title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **APC_LEVEL** | IRQL 1: asynchronous procedure calls run here; holding a fast mutex raises to it. (3.02) |
| **Attestation signing** | Microsoft signing a driver package submitted through the Partner Center, without hardware tests. (5.04) |
| **Bug check** | The system stopping because kernel code failed; the blue screen, with a code and four parameters. (1.05) |
| **Buffered I/O** | The I/O manager copying user data through a kernel system buffer. (2.04) |
| **Callback (notification)** | A driver function registered with a documented API, called on events such as process creation. (4.01) |
| **Catalog (.cat)** | A signed list of hashes of a driver package's files. (5.04) |
| **CONTAINING_RECORD** | Computes the address of a structure from the address of one of its members. (3.05) |
| **CTL_CODE** | The macro that builds an IOCTL's 32-bit code from device type, function, method and access. (2.03) |
| **Device object** | The object requests are sent to; a driver creates one and names it under \Device. (2.01) |
| **Direct I/O** | Locking the user's pages and describing them with an MDL instead of copying. (2.04) |
| **DISPATCH_LEVEL** | IRQL 2: DPCs and spin-lock holders run here; no waiting, no paged memory. (3.02) |
| **Dispatch routine** | The driver function that handles one kind of IRP (create, read, device control...). (2.02) |
| **DPC** | Deferred procedure call: a function queued to run soon at DISPATCH_LEVEL. (3.04) |
| **Driver object** | The object representing a loaded driver, with its dispatch table and Unload routine. (1.04) |
| **Driver Verifier** | A built-in tool that checks selected drivers and makes their bugs fail immediately. (5.01) |
| **DriverEntry** | A driver's entry point, called once when it is loaded. (1.04) |
| **ETW** | Event Tracing for Windows: the system-wide high-speed tracing infrastructure. (4.02) |
| **Fast mutex** | A lock for PASSIVE_LEVEL code that sleeps instead of spinning. (3.03) |
| **INF** | The text file that describes how to install a driver package. (5.04) |
| **IOCTL** | An I/O control request: a driver's own operations, sent with DeviceIoControl. (2.03) |
| **IRP** | I/O request packet: the structure carrying one request to a driver. (2.02) |
| **IRQL** | Interrupt request level: decides what code may run and do on a processor at a moment. (3.02) |
| **KDNET** | Kernel debugging over the network between host and target. (1.02) |
| **KMDF / UMDF** | Microsoft's kernel-mode and user-mode driver frameworks on top of WDM. (1.03) |
| **LIST_ENTRY** | The kernel's intrusive doubly linked list link. (3.05) |
| **Lookaside list** | A cache of freed fixed-size blocks for fast reuse. (3.05) |
| **MDL** | Memory descriptor list: describes the physical pages of a locked buffer. (2.04) |
| **METHOD_NEITHER** | Passing raw user pointers to the driver; best avoided. (2.04) |
| **Non-paged pool** | Kernel memory that is never paged out; required at DISPATCH_LEVEL and above. (3.01) |
| **NTSTATUS** | The 32-bit result of kernel functions; negative means failure. (1.03) |
| **Paged pool** | Kernel memory that can be paged out; only for PASSIVE_LEVEL and APC_LEVEL code. (3.01) |
| **PASSIVE_LEVEL** | IRQL 0: normal thread execution; everything is allowed. (3.02) |
| **Pending IRP** | A request marked pending and completed later; must be cancellable and finished before unload. (2.02) |
| **Pool tag** | Four characters attached to each pool allocation, used to find leaks and owners. (3.01) |
| **SAL** | Source annotation language: annotations that let analysis check buffers, IRQLs and results. (5.02) |
| **SDDL** | Security descriptor definition language, used to say who may open a device. (2.01) |
| **Special pool** | Verifier's allocator that puts each block against a guard page to catch overruns. (5.01) |
| **Spin lock** | A lock that busy-waits at DISPATCH_LEVEL; held only briefly. (3.03) |
| **Symbolic link** | A name in \?? that points to a device so user mode can open it as \\.\Name. (2.01) |
| **Test signing** | A development mode that loads drivers signed with a test certificate; only in the lab VM. (1.02) |
| **UNICODE_STRING** | The kernel's counted UTF-16 string, with lengths in bytes. (1.03) |
| **Unload** | The routine that undoes everything DriverEntry did, in reverse order. (1.04) |
| **WDK** | Windows Driver Kit: headers, libraries, tools and templates for building drivers. (1.03) |
| **WinDbg** | Microsoft's debugger, used for kernel debugging and crash dumps. (1.05) |
| **Work item** | Work queued to run at PASSIVE_LEVEL in a system worker thread. (3.04) |
